Sensitivity analysis for publication bias on the SROC curve

srocsa.t.Rd

This function conducts the likelihood-based sensitivity analysis for publication bias on the summary receiver operating characteristic (SROC) curve and the area under the SROC curve (SAUC) in meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy (Zhou et al., 2023). The bivariate random-effects model of the logit-transformed sensitivity and specificity is combined with a selection function on the \(t\)-statistic of the linear combination of them with the contrast vector \((c_1, c_2)\). The model is fitted for each marginal selection probability \(p\) in sa.p.

Usage

srocsa.t(
  TP,
  FN,
  TN,
  FP,
  data = NULL,
  cc.value = 0.5,
  cc.type = c("single", "all"),
  sa.p = 0.9,
  c11 = NULL,
  ci.level = 0.95,
  parallel.ncores = 1L,
  parset = list()
)

Arguments

TP

Specify the column of true positives (TP).

FN

Specify the column of false negatives (FN).

TN

Specify the column of true negatives (TN).

FP

Specify the column of false positives (FP).

data

A data frame containing the columns of TP, FN, TN, and FP. One row corresponds to one study. It is required.

cc.value

Value added to the cells for the “continuity correction”, within (0, 1]. The default is 0.5.

cc.type

Type of the “continuity correction” (c("single", "all")). The default is "single". "single": cc.value is added to all the cells of the studies with at least one zero cell. "all": cc.value is added to all the cells of all the studies if at least one study has a zero cell.

sa.p

A numeric vector of the marginal selection probabilities \(p = P(\mathrm{select})\), within (0, 1]. The model is fitted for each value. \(p = 1\) indicates no publication bias, and \(\beta\) and \(\alpha\) are not estimated. The default is 0.9.

c11

Pre-specified value of \(c_1^2\) within [0, 1] (\(c_2^2 = 1 - c_1^2\)). If c11 = NULL (default), \(c_1^2\) is estimated together with the other parameters.

ci.level

The confidence level of the confidence intervals, within (0, 1). The default is 0.95.

parallel.ncores

The number of cores used for the parallel computation over sa.p (PSOCK cluster of the package parallel). The default is 1L (no parallel computation).

parset

A list of the settings for the estimation, which updates the default settings. Bad bounds may cause non-convergence.

  • mu.bound: \(\mu_1\) and \(\mu_2\) are searched within [-mu.bound, mu.bound]. The default is 5.

  • tau.bound: \(\tau_1\) and \(\tau_2\) are searched within [eps, tau.bound]. The default is 5.

  • beta.interval: The lower and upper bounds of \(\beta\). The default is c(0, 5).

  • alpha.bound: The root of \(\alpha\) is searched starting from the interval [-alpha.bound, alpha.bound], which is extended if necessary (see uniroot). The default is 5.

  • eps: The lower bound of \(\tau_1\) and \(\tau_2\). The default is 1e-5.

The element inital.values is not used in this function.

Value

An object of class "srocsa": a list with one element for each value of sa.p and the element call. Each element is the output of nlminb (par is (mu1, mu2, tau1, tau2, rho, beta), followed by c11 when c11 = NULL) with the following additional elements, or NULL if the estimation failed.

var.ml

The inverse of the numerical Hessian matrix of the negative log-likelihood. When \(p = 1\), only for (mu1, mu2, tau1, tau2, rho).

sauc.ci

SAUC and its confidence interval.

beta, alpha

The estimates of \(\beta\) and \(\alpha\) (NA when \(p = 1\)).

mu1.ci, mu2.ci

The estimates and confidence intervals of \(\mu_1\) and \(\mu_2\), and of the sensitivity and specificity.

par.all

All the estimates: mu1, mu2, tau1^2, tau2^2, tau12, c1^2, c2^2, beta, alpha, sauc, sens, spec.

The attribute "data" is a data frame of the study-level logit-transformed sensitivity (y1) and specificity (y2) and their variances (v1, v2), used by plot.srocsa (add.study = TRUE). The results can be shown by print.srocsa, summary.srocsa, and plot.srocsa.

Details

Bivariate model

Let \(y_{1i}\) and \(y_{2i}\) be the logit-transformed sensitivity and specificity of study \(i\), and \(v_{1i}\) and \(v_{2i}\) be their variances. \((y_{1i}, y_{2i})\) follows the bivariate normal distribution with mean \((\mu_1, \mu_2)\) and variance-covariance matrix \(\mathrm{diag}(v_{1i}, v_{2i}) + \Omega\), where \(\Omega\) has the between-study standard deviations \(\tau_1, \tau_2\) and correlation \(\rho\).

Selection function

The probability of publishing study \(i\) is modeled as \(\Phi(\alpha + \beta t_i)\), where \(t_i = (c_1 y_{1i} + c_2 y_{2i}) / \sqrt{c_1^2 v_{1i} + c_2^2 v_{2i}}\), \(c_1, c_2 \ge 0\), and \(c_1^2 + c_2^2 = 1\). For given \(p\) and the other parameters, \(\alpha\) is determined such that the mean of the inverse of the marginal selection probabilities of the observed studies equals \(1/p\).

SAUC

See sauc.

Initial values

The initial values of \((\mu_1, \mu_2, \tau_1, \tau_2, \rho)\) are the estimates of the bivariate model without selection by mixmeta. The initial values of \(\beta\) and \(c_1^2\) are 0.1.

Continuity correction

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continuity_correction

References

Zhou Y, Huang A, Hattori S (2023). A likelihood-based sensitivity analysis for publication bias on the summary receiver operating characteristic in meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy. Statistics in Medicine, 42(6), 781–798. doi:10.1002/sim.9643

See also

print.srocsa, summary.srocsa, plot.srocsa, reitsma.sroc, sauc

Examples

## load data
data(IVD)

## estimate c1^2
fit1 <- srocsa.t(TP = TP, FN = FN, TN = TN, FP = FP, data = IVD, sa.p = c(1, 0.8, 0.6))
fit1
#> ==================================================
#> Model optimization
#> 
#> Number of studies : 33 
#> Optimizer         : 1 1 1 
#>
